question: Given an already known public two-point relation, can one construct a good-reduction rational curve and lifts on which the identical coefficients give an exact relation?
source_panel: all distinct-x public relation hits in experiments/xedni-hensel-fresh-transfer-20261118/run-result.json.gz, in original event order
input_condition: nonzero b with gcd(b,q)=1; retain every excluded or failed row
construction: R=[b^-1 mod q]U; check V=[-a]R; choose centered integer coordinates x,y of R; set A=-1 and B=y^2-x^3-Ax; T=(x,y); P1=[b]T, P2=[-a]T
checks: curve nonsingular over Q and good reduction to y^2=x^3-x-2 mod p; R reduces correctly; P1 and P2 reduce to U,V; aP1+bP2=O exactly; independent replay all input rows
claim_boundary: constructive existence conditional on the public relation coefficients already being known; no relation-discovery or cost claim
